subtopics.name: Ecosystem as a functional unit of nature
Structure of an ecosystem: abiotic and biotic components and stratification
Functional aspects of an ecosystem: productivity, decomposition, energy flow and nutrient cycling

Producers and consumers in food chains and food webs
Grazing food chain and detritus food chain
Trophic levels, standing crop and the ten per cent law
Ecological pyramids of number, biomass and energy
Inverted pyramids and why the pyramid of energy is always upright

note: The headings list starts at 12.1, so the chapter-opening passages (P01 the "CHAPTER 12" heading, P02 the chapter title, P03-P04 the introduction) have no numbered heading; from_heading is "unsure" for that subtopic, and the chapter summary (P37) and exercises (P38), which range over the whole chapter, are attached to it so every passage is covered. Section 12.4 (Energy flow) is long and carries several distinct testable ideas - solar input and thermodynamics, producers/consumers, GFC versus DFC, and trophic levels with the ten per cent law - so it was split into four subtopics; 12.5 was split into the pyramids themselves, the exceptions/inverted pyramids, and their limitations.
